paper.title: Self-organization and a dynamical transition in traffic-flow models

headline: Biham-Middleton-Levine 1992 traffic (two-species CA): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; free-flow->gridlock transition at rho_c=0.365 (v crosses 0.5), near-step width=0.089 (v: 0.9->0.1) on an L=128 grid

verdicts.gate: P1 free-flow->gridlock transition: rho_c (v crosses 0.5) in [0.3, 0.4], v~1 low-rho, v~0 high-rho
P2 two-phase order: v(rho=0.2) >= 0.95 (free flow) AND v(rho=0.55) <= 0.05 (gridlock)
P3 near-step: density width where v drops 0.9 -> 0.1 is <= 0.15

extra.framing: two-species traffic CELLULAR AUTOMATON (CA, disclosed) on a periodic grid: red moves east / blue north on alternating ticks; a car moves iff its target is empty in the frozen grid; the only randomness is the seeded initial placement, the update is a deterministic synchronous rule — NOT agent-stepping
extra.metastability: finite-size metastability is expected near the transition (long-lived partially-jammed states, bimodal seeds); L=128, long warm-up and tail+seed averaging are used and residual smearing is reported honestly, not hidden
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the BML self-organizing jamming PHASE TRANSITION (velocity 1->0 near-step at rho_c in [0.30,0.40]) and would catch an artifact

citations: Biham, O., Middleton, A.A. & Levine, D. (1992). Self-organization and a dynamical transition in traffic-flow models. Physical Review A 46(10):R6124-R6127. doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.46.R6124.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the BML jamming transition (rho_c, free/jam limits, near-step width)
